title: Claims Adjudication Basis: What a Medicare Supplement Policy Pays on a Crossover Line
content:
The supplement pays the share of the Medicare cost sharing its plan letter covers, always worked out from the amount Medicare approved and never from what the provider billed. This is the adjudication basis for every policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies.

### Conditions before a line is paid

1. **Cover on the day of service.** The policy stands as active or in its grace period on the date of service of the line. The status, the policy and the day it took effect are read from the policy record, correlated by that policy, before the line is processed.

2. **Medicare has decided first.** Medicare has made its own determination on the claim and the amount Medicare approved is recorded on the crossover line. The line, the number Medicare gave the claim, the approved amount and the status the line stands at are what establish this, correlated by that crossover line, before the line is processed.

### The quantities the share is taken on

The Medicare cost sharing on a line is the amount Medicare approved less what Medicare paid on it, and never less than nothing. The supplement pays the share of that cost sharing the plan letter covers, rounded to the cent. What remains of an annual high deductible is the plan letter's high deductible less what the policyholder has already accrued toward it in the calendar year, never less than nothing, and it is taken from the share before the payment is made.

### Benefits the letter does not carry

A benefit the plan letter does not cover is not paid at all, and the line is denied on the ground that the benefit is not in the plan rather than paid in part; the policyholder is told which of the standardised plans would have covered it.

### Excess charges

Excess charges arise only where the provider does not accept Medicare assignment, so a policyholder complaining of a balance bill from an assigned provider is told that the bill is wrong rather than that their plan does not cover it.

### Annual limits and deductibles

On a plan letter with an annual out-of-pocket limit the supplement pays everything once the policyholder's own payments reach that limit for the calendar year.

> **No longer in force.** The following clause of this basis has been superseded by the current basis and is no longer in force; it is set out here only so that it is never applied: "On a high-deductible plan letter the supplement pays nothing until the policyholder's own payments for the calendar year reach the high deductible, and from that point it pays as the standard plan letter would."

### Foreign travel and waiting periods

Foreign travel emergency care is paid after its own yearly deductible, at the plan letter's coinsurance, and only up to the lifetime maximum; once that maximum is reached further foreign claims are denied and the policyholder is told so before they travel again.

A condition treated in the six months before issue is not covered during the plan letter's waiting period, unless the policyholder had creditable coverage and the letter waives it on that ground.
